drafted_from: tool:match-colour's own row in tools/media-composition/tool-rows.json, tools/media-composition/do-work/grade-a-video.mjs (the script this tool runs with only the match options), and the script run on a synthetic 7 second clip and a 26 second test-pattern clip
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make my second camera video match the colour of my first camera video at 8 seconds in." It runs tool:match-colour and saves the matched video in your files.
no_lists_because: It makes a new video in your files from the video you name and keeps no list of its own.
instructions: 1. Find the identities in your files of the video to change (video) and of the video whose colour to copy (match_to).
2. Say "Match this video's colour to that one". Add match_at, the seconds into match_to to take its colour from (default 0).

3. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run and tool tool:match-colour. The door runs it in a container and answers {"result": {...}}; an error comes back as {"error": "what to change"}.
4. Read result (duration_seconds, width, height, bytes) and files.video, the matched video in your files at its own size and length. To grade it further, run tool:grade-a-video on that new video.

worked_examples.title: One clip matched to the colour of another at 8 seconds
worked_examples.ask: Make this clip match the colour of my main camera at 8 seconds in.
worked_examples.given: read from tools/media-composition/do-work/grade-a-video.mjs and run on a 7 second 320x180 clip matched to a 26 second test-pattern clip at 8 seconds; no look is applied, so looks is empty
